Package io.webagent4j.policy.network

Interface INetworkAddressAuthority

public interface INetworkAddressAuthority
Capability an INetworkPolicy may additionally implement to expose the exact, freshly resolved and individually-authorized IP address set for one destination, so a transport can bind its actual connection to that same set instead of performing its own, independent resolution that could silently observe a different result between the check and the connection - the DNS rebinding / time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap this interface exists to close.

Not every INetworkPolicy can offer this: a fully custom policy that never resolves addresses at all has nothing to authorize, and simply does not implement this interface. A caller that finds no INetworkAddressAuthority for its configured policy falls back to an ordinary, unpinned connection - no worse than this package's pre-existing behavior, and documented in package-info.java as this package's honest boundary: it is not a complete SSRF firewall for arbitrary policies.

For a policy that implements this interface, authorizeConnection(io.webagent4j.policy.network.NetworkDestination) is the complete authorization decision for one connection attempt on its own - a caller does not, and must not, also call IExecutionPolicy.evaluate(C) for that same attempt first. Calling both would resolve the destination twice, leaving a real (if narrow) window for a DNS-rebinding attacker to answer the two resolutions differently; authorizeConnection(io.webagent4j.policy.network.NetworkDestination) already applies every rule evaluate would; a present result here is exactly as authoritative as an ALLOW from evaluate would have been, at the cost of at most one resolver observation for the attempt. A caller that receives Optional.empty() from authorizeConnection(io.webagent4j.policy.network.NetworkDestination) must treat that as this connection attempt being denied - fail closed, never a silent fall back to an unpinned connection, since that would defeat the very guarantee this interface exists to provide.

  • Method Details

    • authorizeConnection

      Optional<VerifiedNetworkAddresses> authorizeConnection(NetworkDestination destination)
      Resolves and authorizes destination for one connection attempt - the complete authorization decision for that attempt, on its own.

      Implementations perform at most one resolution per call - no hidden retry, exactly like INetworkAddressResolver - and apply the same scheme/host/port/userinfo and address-category rules IExecutionPolicy.evaluate(C) would apply to the same destination, so this call needs no separate, preceding evaluate call for the same attempt: a present result here already means this exact address set is authorized, exactly as an ALLOW from evaluate would have meant. Returns Optional.empty() when resolution fails, yields no addresses, the destination fails any of the policy's own scheme/host/port/userinfo rules, or any resolved address is denied by an address-category rule - fail closed, never a partially filtered address set; a caller treats an empty result as the connection being denied.

      Parameters:
      destination - the textual destination to resolve and authorize; never itself resolved
      Returns:
      the authorized address set, or Optional.empty() when authorization fails
